newsitem.title: USA: "Underground Railroad" to have museum in U.S..
newsitem.headline: "Underground Railroad" to have museum in U.S..

text.p: Officials of a new foundation said Monday they planned to build an $80 million museum honouring the "Underground Railroad", a secret network of people who helped runaway slaves before the Civil War.
The newly formed National Underground Railroad Freedom Centre "will stand as a beacon of freedom in Cincinnati," civil rights leader Vernon Jordan said in a statement.

From about 1830 to 1860, people who opposed slavery often hid fugitives in their homes as the runaways made their way from the southern slaveholding states to the northern free states where slavery had been abolished, or to Canada.
Cincinnati, just across the Ohio River from Kentucky, was "a haven on the critical dividing line between the slave South and the free North," Jordan said.
A $3 million gift from Cincinnati-based consumer products giant Procter & Gamble Co. will help launch the centre, to open in 2002, Edwin Rigaud, the Freedom Center's executive director, said.

"This gift will allow us to begin the research to tell stories of the runaway slaves and the other people of good will who risked everything to secure safe passage for those seeking freedom," he said.
Rigaud is an executive on loan from P&G, maker of Tide detergent and Crest toothpaste.

The center's national advisory board also includes executives of Xerox Corp., Lockheed Martin Corp., Black Enterprise Magazine, Halliburton Co., Sara Lee Corp., Federated Department Stores Inc. and other companies, as well as Cincinnati Mayor Roxanne Qualls and other local officials.
